videos.title: Connect your robot arms
videos.subtitle: Pretend arms, real arms, and the STOP button

lines.maya: Hi Ms. Nova! I just got my robot arms. How do I start?

lines.nova: Hi Maya! Welcome to GRIP. Your kit has two arms. The leader is the one you move with your hand, and the follower copies you.

lines.maya: Can I try it without plugging anything in?

lines.nova: Yes! Click Use a pretend arm on the leader card, and then on the follower card.
With real arms, you click Connect both arms and pick the USB ports instead. Now turn on the follower's motors.

lines.maya: What's the big red button at the top?

lines.nova: That's STOP. If anything looks wrong, press STOP, or the Escape key. Robot rule number one: hands clear, then press go!

lines.maya: Got it! Hands clear, then go.
How do I make Pip move?

lines.nova: Open the Drive tab and try a pose button. Let's press Wave up!

lines.maya: It waved! I can see it in the 3D view, too.

lines.nova: Each joint has its own card. Press plus to turn it ten degrees. Zero is the middle.
Press Open, then Close. In real life, only grab soft and light things.
Exactly! Start on slow speed while you practice. You're a robot pilot now.

videos.title: Code with blocks
videos.subtitle: Make Pip do a whole show by itself

click.name: Try it on a pretend arm

lines.maya: Can I make Pip do a whole show by itself?

lines.nova: Yes, with code! Blocks snap together like puzzle pieces, and Pip runs them from top to bottom.
This program makes Pip wave. Press Go, and watch which block lights up.

lines.maya: The block lights up while it runs!

lines.nova: Now pick Surprise show from Start from, and press Go again.

lines.maya: Pip talks and plays sounds! Is it different every time?

lines.nova: Yes! The Surprise blocks pick random numbers. Press Show me the code to see the same program written in Python.

lines.maya: Whoa, real code! I'm a programmer.

lines.nova: Yes! Press Start Copy me. When you move the leader arm, the follower copies you.
With pretend arms, these sliders are your hand on the leader. Let's turn the base.

lines.maya: It copies me, like a mirror!

lines.nova: Now record a demo. Press Record, move slowly, then press Save.
Great job! Record five demos of the same task, starting from the same spot, so the robot brain can learn it.

videos.title: Train a robot brain
videos.subtitle: Learning from demos, then testing like a scientist

lines.maya: I recorded three demos of a wave. What now?

lines.nova: Open the Train tab and press Start learning. Pip's brain practices guessing the next move.
That line shows the mistakes. Lower is better. Now open Try it, and press Go.

lines.maya: Pip did it all by itself!

lines.nova: It did! Now test it ten times and count the wins, like a real scientist. That's how engineers make robots better.
